items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: It was Budd Johnson and Gene Ramey, we played with him.

ctx.x: A couple of different recordings I wanted to ask you about. You played with Earl Hines?

Oh that was something. That “Live at the Vanguard.” That’s one of my favorite things that I made. It was almost the same kind of thing. He was the nicest man. The nicest guy. I mean whooh. He was the nicest person, oh man. And we never rehearsed. I never rehearsed with him either. It was Budd Johnson and Gene Ramey, we played with him. That was quite an experience. He was dynamic. He was so dynamic on that piano, it was just like whooh. It was like a whole band. You never knew what he was going to do. You had to…

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Locke were playing together with Tyree over there.

ctx.x: : What was you doing upstairs, the belly dancers or something?
No, we were in the main room, but Tyree and them had a -- and Arvell Shaw and Jake -- the Hanna guy, Roland Hanna and Eddie Locke were playing together with Tyree over there.
